topics.label: Welcome and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Traditional cancer treatment modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine foundational cancer treatments including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their mechanisms, toxicities, and limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular and genetic vulnerabilities in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic driver kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and addressing subsequent challenges of resistance, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design and mechanisms of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates used to target cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system interacts with cancer and detail immunotherapeutic strategies such as immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical trends, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address broader issues in oncology including genomic stratification, historical survival trends, early detection, and ethical dilemmas in therapy management.
